title: From research question to reviewable artifact
text:
Purpose
The research-writing framework in this repository makes recurring literature work executable: retrieve candidate papers, apply metadata-based screening, produce a synthesis, assemble a source-linked draft, and optionally open a review PR.
Quarto is the publication layer, not the agent orchestrator. The workflow remains in LangGraph and runs independently of website rendering.

title: From research question to reviewable artifact
text:
Architecture





flowchart LR
    Search[Search] --> Screen[Screen]
    Screen --> Synthesize[Synthesize]
    Synthesize --> Store[Bundle]
    Store --> Publish[Review PR]













Stage
Responsibility




Search
Retrieve candidate metadata from arXiv and Semantic Scholar


Screen
Deduplicate and rank using venue, citation, and recency heuristics


Synthesize
Use the configured model, or deterministic no-LLM drafting


Bundle
Write a Quarto article, bibliography, source records, and social-copy sidecar


Publish
On explicit request, prepare a research-branch site change and open a PR

title: From research question to reviewable artifact
text:
Autonomy and publication are separate
The configured workflow progresses through its stages without new approval prompts between them. By default, it writes a local draft and performs no Git publication. A requested non-dry run can open a PR containing the intended site page, but it does not merge or deploy.
That boundary lets the research workflow remain autonomous without treating unreviewed output as approved public content.

title: From research question to reviewable artifact
text:
Traceable artifacts
The source record travels alongside the draft. The publishing path checks an explicit file set, protects existing destinations, and refuses unrelated Git changes. The website build validates local links, bibliography resolution, publication paths, and output boundaries without making model calls.
Tests exercise document serialization, filesystem boundaries, rendered citations, temporary-repository publication, and the configured graph with controlled retrieval inputs.

title: From research question to reviewable artifact
text:
Current limits
The present writer works from truncated abstracts and metadata. Its screening scores are discovery heuristics, not scientific-quality assessments. A draft is therefore labeled unverified. The framework does not currently implement or validate original experiments, establish novelty, or certify its conclusions.
Future improvements can add full-text extraction, stronger source checking, and new research stages while preserving explicit state and provenance.

title: UMatch: matching over streaming data
text: Source code ↗ Recorded demo ↗ Slides ↗

title: UMatch: matching over streaming data
text:
The problem
UMatch explores matching ride requests to nearby drivers within a streaming window. The engineering challenge begins before the matching step: historical taxi-trip records describe completed trips, rather than continuously available drivers and waiting riders.
The repository’s documented design constructs separate rider and driver-location streams, then joins plausible candidates for matching. The existing project record uses Python, Kafka, Spark Structured Streaming, and a presentation layer.

title: UMatch: matching over streaming data
text:
Three design decisions

1. Construct the input streams
The project uses taxi-trip records and synthetic information to simulate two unbounded streams. Timestamps provide a basis for processing windows, but they do not provide a shared rider/driver identity key.


2. Narrow the candidate join
An unrestricted Cartesian join compares every rider with every driver in a window. The documented approach instead introduces location-based keys through geohashes, grouping geographically nearby candidates before matching.


3. Apply greedy distance matching
Within those groups, the project applies a greedy assignment using a Haversine-distance condition. This is an engineering trade-off rather than a claim of globally optimal matching. Group boundaries, windowing, unmatched requests, and local density are relevant to interpreting the approach.

title: UMatch: matching over streaming data

title: UMatch: matching over streaming data
section: What a fuller evaluation should document
text:
What a fuller evaluation should document
A reproducible evaluation would identify data selection and simulation rules, window sizes, grouping parameters, workload density, baselines, hardware, and matching quality as well as latency. The repository includes historical project material, but this page does not turn it into a newly reproduced benchmark.

Current record: engineering project with source, architecture, slides, and a demonstration. Numerical results and independent use should be added only with their supporting records.
